nodes.label: ADR-003: Asynq on Redis for Background Job Queue
nodes.rationale: Synchronous email sending in HTTP handlers would couple response latency to Resend API availability and provide no retry mechanism. Asynq on the already-required Redis instance was chosen over a DB-polling worker or a dedicated MQ (RabbitMQ/SQS) because it needs no new infrastructure and provides built-in retry/DLQ. Trade-off: Asynq's `asynq:*` keys share Redis with session/rate-limit data under an `allkeys-lru` eviction policy, risking eviction of queued jobs under memory pressure if queue volume grows; a separate worker binary (`apps/backend/cmd/worker/`) must be deployed and monitored independently.
